chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Fadala and Ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr and Jamil, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"What Allah has forbidden in the Quran from among moving creatures is only the pig, but it is the one of unknown [origin]."

key_terms.النَّكَرَةُ: the unknown/strange one (referring to the pig's distinct status)

ai.seo_question: Why is the pig specifically singled out as the only forbidden creature in the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir clarifies that while the Quran explicitly names the pig as forbidden, its designation as 'an-nakarah' (the unknown or distinct one) highlights its unique categorical status among all creatures. This distinction underscores the principle that explicit textual prohibition in the Quran carries a specific weight, whereas other impurities are derived through scholarly deduction (ijtihad) or prophetic tradition. The reference to 'an-nakarah' invites scholarly discussion on whether this term denotes the pig's singular mention or its inherent impurity (najis) distinct from other edible animals.
